Data Warehousing and Mining (DWM) — Experiment 03¶

Experiment Title: Data Preprocessing, Exploration and Visualization¶

Dataset: stock_market_data.csv (3 Years of Daily NSE Trading Data across 20 Major Indian Stocks & 5 Sectors)

1. Objectives¶

  • Perform comprehensive data preprocessing, type normalization, and temporal feature engineering on the multi-sector Indian stock market trading dataset.
  • Conduct exploratory data analysis (EDA) and statistical aggregation to understand price distributions, daily returns, trading volumes, and intraday volatility.
  • Build multi-dimensional visualizations across stocks, sectors, and time horizons to uncover liquidity patterns, risk-return characteristics, outliers, and feature correlations.
  • Prepare and validate the dataset for downstream data mining tasks (regression, classification, clustering, and association rule mining).

7. Preprocessing & Feature Engineering¶

  • Convert Date to datetime format.
  • Extract temporal features: Year, Month, MonthName, and DayOfWeek.
  • Derive Intraday_Volatility as $\frac{\text{High\_Price} - \text{Low\_Price}}{\text{Open\_Price}} \times 100$.
  • Verify cleaned dataset dimensions and preview the transformed table.
# Convert Date to datetime
df['Date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['Date'])

# Extract temporal attributes
df['Year'] = df['Date'].dt.year
df['Month'] = df['Date'].dt.month
df['MonthName'] = df['Date'].dt.month_name()
df['DayOfWeek'] = df['Date'].dt.day_name()

# Derive Intraday Volatility (%)
df['Intraday_Volatility'] = (((df['High_Price'] - df['Low_Price']) / df['Open_Price']) * 100).round(2)

print("Cleaned & Engineered Dataset Shape:", df.shape)
df.head()

8. Stock-wise Trading Volume Analysis¶

Aggregate total trading volume per Ticker, display the top 10 most actively traded stocks, and visualize them with a horizontal bar chart.

top_10_volume = (
    df.groupby(['Ticker', 'Sector'], as_index=False)['Volume']
    .sum()
    .sort_values(by='Volume', ascending=False)
    .head(10)
    .reset_index(drop=True)
)

print("Top 10 Most Actively Traded Stocks (3-Year Cumulative Volume):")
display(top_10_volume)

plt.figure(figsize=(11, 6))
ax = sns.barplot(
    data=top_10_volume,
    x='Volume',
    y='Ticker',
    hue='Sector',
    dodge=False,
    palette='viridis'
)
plt.title('Top 10 Stocks by Trading Volume')
plt.xlabel('Cumulative Trading Volume (Shares)')
plt.ylabel('Stock Ticker')
plt.legend(title='Sector', loc='lower right')

plt.show()

9. Sector-wise Performance & Market Representation¶

Group by Sector to compute total trading volume, average daily return, and average intraday volatility, followed by a horizontal bar chart of total volume by sector.

sector_summary = (
    df.groupby('Sector', as_index=False)
    .agg(
        Total_Volume=('Volume', 'sum'),
        Avg_Daily_Return=('Daily_Return', 'mean'),
        Avg_Intraday_Volatility=('Intraday_Volatility', 'mean'),
        Avg_Close_Price=('Close_Price', 'mean')
    )
    .sort_values(by='Total_Volume', ascending=False)
    .reset_index(drop=True)
)
sector_summary['Avg_Daily_Return'] = sector_summary['Avg_Daily_Return'].round(4)
sector_summary['Avg_Intraday_Volatility'] = sector_summary['Avg_Intraday_Volatility'].round(2)
sector_summary['Avg_Close_Price'] = sector_summary['Avg_Close_Price'].round(2)

print("Sector-wise Performance Summary:")
display(sector_summary)

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
sns.barplot(
    data=sector_summary,
    x='Total_Volume',
    y='Sector',
    hue='Sector',
    palette='magma',
    legend=False
)
plt.title('Total Trading Volume by Sector')
plt.xlabel('Total Trading Volume (Shares)')
plt.ylabel('Sector')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

10. Temporal Trend Analysis¶

Compute monthly average closing price and monthly cumulative trading volume across the 3-year window, and plot the Monthly Market Volume Trend.

df['YearMonth'] = df['Date'].dt.to_period('M').astype(str)

monthly_trend = (
    df.groupby('YearMonth', as_index=False)
    .agg(
        Avg_Close_Price=('Close_Price', 'mean'),
        Total_Monthly_Volume=('Volume', 'sum'),
        Avg_Daily_Return=('Daily_Return', 'mean')
    )
    .sort_values('YearMonth')
)
monthly_trend['Avg_Close_Price'] = monthly_trend['Avg_Close_Price'].round(2)
monthly_trend['Avg_Daily_Return'] = monthly_trend['Avg_Daily_Return'].round(3)

print("Monthly Trend Sample (First 10 Months):")
display(monthly_trend.head(10))

plt.figure(figsize=(13, 6))
sns.lineplot(
    data=monthly_trend,
    x='YearMonth',
    y='Total_Monthly_Volume',
    marker='o',
    linewidth=2.2,
    color='#1f77b4'
)
plt.title('Monthly Market Volume Trend')
plt.xlabel('Year-Month')
plt.ylabel('Total Monthly Trading Volume (Shares)')
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

  • Generate a boxplot of Intraday_Volatility across sectors and overall market.
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(15, 6))

# Boxplot 1: Daily_Return by Sector
sns.boxplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sector',
    y='Daily_Return',
    hue='Sector',
    palette='Set2',
    legend=False,
    ax=axes[0]
)
axes[0].axhline(0, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=1)
axes[0].set_title('Distribution of Daily Return by Sector')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Sector')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Daily Return (%)')

# Boxplot 2: Intraday_Volatility
sns.boxplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sector',
    y='Intraday_Volatility',
    hue='Sector',
    palette='Set3',
    legend=False,
    ax=axes[1]
)
axes[1].set_title('Distribution of Intraday Volatility by Sector')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Sector')
axes[1].set_ylabel('Intraday Volatility (%)')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

12. Relationship & Correlation Analysis¶

  • Plot a scatter plot comparing Volume vs Daily_Return with alpha transparency to examine volume-return dynamics.
  • Plot a correlation heatmap of numerical features (Open_Price, High_Price, Low_Price, Close_Price, Volume, Daily_Return, Intraday_Volatility).
plt.figure(figsize=(11, 6))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Volume',
    y='Daily_Return',
    hue='Sector',
    alpha=0.45,
    s=35,
    palette='tab10'
)
plt.axhline(0, color='black', linestyle='--', linewidth=1)
plt.xscale('log')
plt.title('Trading Volume (Log Scale) vs Daily Return (%)')
plt.xlabel('Trading Volume (Log Scale)')
plt.ylabel('Daily Return (%)')
plt.legend(title='Sector', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

numerical_cols = [
    'Open_Price', 'High_Price', 'Low_Price', 'Close_Price',
    'Volume', 'Daily_Return', 'Intraday_Volatility'
]

corr_matrix = df[numerical_cols].corr()

plt.figure(figsize=(9, 7))
sns.heatmap(
    corr_matrix,
    annot=True,
    fmt='.2f',
    cmap='coolwarm',
    vmin=-1,
    vmax=1,
    linewidths=0.5,
    square=True
)
plt.title('Correlation Heatmap of Numerical Stock Features')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

13. Summary of Findings & Conclusion¶

Key Behavioral Insights:¶

  1. Data Completeness & Quality: The dataset comprises 14,800 records (20 major NSE stocks $\times$ 740 trading days over 3 years) with zero missing values and zero duplicate records.
  2. Liquidity & Volume Concentration: Trading volume is heavily concentrated in lower-denomination, high-liquidity large-cap stocks across the Energy (NTPC, POWERGRID, ONGC, RELIANCE), Banking (HDFCBANK, SBIN, ICICIBANK), and FMCG (ITC) sectors.
  3. Sectoral Volatility & Fat Tails:
    • Daily_Return across all five sectors is centered near $0\%$, exhibiting symmetric leptokurtic (fat-tailed) distributions typical of equity markets.
    • Auto, Energy, and IT show slightly higher median Intraday_Volatility and wider interquartile ranges compared to defensive FMCG stocks (HINDUNILVR, NESTLEIND, BRITANNIA).
  4. Feature Relationships:
    • OHLC prices (Open_Price, High_Price, Low_Price, Close_Price) exhibit near-perfect positive collinearity ($r \approx 1.00$).
    • Extreme positive or negative Daily_Return spikes coincide with elevated Volume and heightened Intraday_Volatility, reflecting institutional participation during earnings announcements and macroeconomic events.

Readiness for Downstream Data Mining Tasks:¶

  • Regression: Clean, continuous OHLC and volatility attributes are ready for next-day price forecasting and return prediction.
  • Classification: Engineered features (Daily_Return, Intraday_Volatility, Volume, temporal attributes) can directly support directional trend classification (Bullish / Bearish / Neutral).
  • Clustering: Sector-level and ticker-level risk-return-liquidity profiles are well-suited for $K$-Means and Hierarchical clustering of market regimes.
  • Association Rule Mining: Discretized sector co-movements and volume-volatility states can be mined via Apriori / FP-Growth to discover cross-sector contagion rules.

14. Auto-export Utility¶

Convert DWM_Lab_3_Stock_Market.ipynb to DWM_Lab_3_Stock_Market.html using nbconvert.

import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

notebook_path = Path("DWM_Lab_3_Stock_Market.ipynb")
if notebook_path.exists():
    cmd = [
        sys.executable, "-m", "jupyter", "nbconvert",
        "--to", "html", "--no-prompt", str(notebook_path)
    ]
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode == 0:
        print("Successfully exported DWM_Lab_3_Stock_Market.html")
    else:
        print("Export notice:", result.stderr)
else:
    print("Notebook file will be exported upon save.")

Successfully exported DWM_Lab_3_Stock_Market.html
